ov: A domesticated omnivore farmed mainly for pork. Pigs were domesticated twice, in the Near East and in China, and around 1.5 billion are raised every year.

why.et: Pork is the main reason pigs are kept, but eating it is forbidden in Islam and Judaism.
why.dg: Mainly wild boar and feral pigs: attacks are rare but can be serious, with 665 recorded victims from 1825 to 2012.
why.p: Farmed mainly for meat, but some are kept as pets.

wt: 140–300 kg for an adult, more in some breeds
rg: Farmed worldwide. Escaped pigs have gone feral in many parts of the world, including the southeastern United States.
df: An omnivore that digs in the soil with its strong, sensitive snout to find food.

cf.tip: A wild boar has a coat of long, coarse bristles over brown under-fur, and its piglets have pale stripes. Farm pigs are only sparsely haired.

fx: An adult pig has 44 teeth, and a male’s canines can grow into tusks that never stop growing.
